sentences.text:
B.A. No.2959 of 2024
 Jitendra Kumar ... Petitioner

Versus
 The State of Jharkhand ... Opposite Party

Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Pradeep Kumar Srivastava
 For the Petitioner : Mr. Rakesh Ranjan, Adv.
 : Mr. Ashok Kr. Jha, Adv.

For the State : Mr. Rakesh Ranjan, Addl. P.P.
 Order No.07/Dated- 12.07.2024
Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. The petitioner has been made an accused in connection with Ranchi Cybercrime P.S. Case No. 47
of 2023 registered for the offences under Sections 120(B)/384/406/419/420/467/468/471 of the
Indian Penal Code and Sections 66(B)/66(C)/66(D) of the Information Technology Act, pending in
the Court of learned A.J.C. II-cum-Special Judge, Cybercrime, Ranchi.
3.  As per FIR, allegation is that on 10.05.2020, informant was contacted via WhatsApp by Shanay Navin, who offered her a work from home job by liking YouTube videos.
Then she was instructed to contact a Telegram app for payment and for further task, after completing the task, informant received some payment.
She continued working and deposited a total sum of Rs. 84,32,100/- into various accounts till 30.05.2023.
Realizing that she had been cheated, she lodged an FIR against Shanay Navin and other unknown cyber criminals.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is further submitted that petitioner is not named in the F.I.R, however, being an account holder, he has been made an accused.
The petitioner is languishing in Judicial Custody since 27.08.2023 without any rhymes and reasons.
Petitioner has no criminal antecedent.
Charge-sheet has been submitted.

Petitioner undertakes to cooperate in the trial of the case by remaining physically present as and when required and shall not indulge in any manner in tampering with the prosecution evidences or influencing the witnesses of prosecution.
Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of bail.

5. On the other hand, learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State has opposed the prayer for bail of the petitioner and submitted that there is huge transaction of money which was grabbed through cheating and cyber fraud.
Investigation is still going on against co-accused persons.

Hence,
petitioner does not deserve bail.

entities.text: Jitendra Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of allegation coupled with the materials available against the petitioner and also in view of the fact that it is case of cybercrime in respect of huge amount and it is alleged that Rs.11,60,000/- has been deposited in the account of the present petitioner through fraud and his account has been freezed.
Investigation against other co-accused persons is still going on.
Although, charge-sheet has been submitted against the present petitioner but investigation against other co-accused persons is still going on to reveal the racket involved in this case.
Under such circumstances, I am not inclined to admit the petitioner on bail at present stage of proceedings which stands rejected.

(Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Sachin Jitendra Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand ... Opposite ... on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119151696/
